best_for: Planners, researchers and GIS analysts who need full desktop mapping and spatial analysis without an ArcGIS license.

points.title: Free from qgis.org
points.text: QGIS is GPL-2.0 and the project says it will always be free when downloaded from qgis.org. It is built by volunteers, companies and agencies, and asks for donations.

points.title: Latest release or LTR
points.text: The project recommends the Long Term Release for most people, because it is tested longer and gets at least a year of fixes. The current LTR is 3.44.15. This site lists the latest release line, 4.2.3.

points.title: QGIS 4 moved to Qt6
points.text: From 4.0 QGIS supports only Qt6, while the 3.44 LTR is still on Qt5. The project notes that some Debian and Ubuntu releases lack the newer dependencies, so they get only the LTR from its repositories.

points.title: Windows: projection grids on demand
points.text: The standalone installer leaves out optional projection grids to stay near 0.5 GiB and asks for them when needed. A 1.2 GiB installer with all grids exists for offline sites. The OSGeo4W installer can keep several versions side by side.

points.title: Mac: one signed installer
points.text: The official macOS installer is signed and notarized and runs on Intel and Apple silicon Macs.

points.title: Linux: Flatpak has the latest only
points.text: The QGIS guide says the Flathub Flatpak covers only the latest stable release, not the LTR; Flathub marks it as verified for qgis.org. For the LTR on Linux, use the project's Debian or Ubuntu repositories.

points.title: Versions here
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 and installs for the whole machine. The Windows listing keeps 23 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
